source.title: How To Match Your Shirt And Tie
source.author: MR PORTER

tips.text: Choose the shirt first, then a tie that picks up one of the colours in it.
tips.why: A shared colour makes the two look coordinated.

tips.text: Pair a bold pattern with a fine one; avoid two patterns of similar scale, such as gingham with a narrow stripe.
tips.why: Patterns of the same size compete and buzz.

tips.text: When both shirt and tie are patterned, make the tie's pattern the larger, bolder one.
tips.why: The tie should lead and the shirt sit behind it.

tips.text: In a formal outfit, keep at least one of the suit, shirt or tie plain.
tips.why: Three patterned pieces together are very hard to pull off.

tips.text: Match tie and shirt texture to the setting: smooth silk and sleek shirting for business, coarser textured fabrics for relaxed occasions.
tips.why: Shine reads formal; texture reads casual.

tips.text: Own a knitted tie; it dresses up with a suit or down with chinos and a cardigan.
tips.why: It covers uncertain dress codes such as some interviews.

tips.text: If you are slim, avoid oversized collars and very wide lapels.
tips.why: Big details overwhelm a slight frame.

tips.text: If you are stocky, avoid skinny ties and narrow collars.
tips.why: Small details make a broad frame look bigger by contrast.

tips.text: Keep tie width in proportion with the lapels and collar; a skinny tie looks wrong under the broad lapels of a double-breasted jacket.
tips.why: Collar, tie and lapel should agree in scale.

tips.text: A thick or heavy tie needs a deeper, larger shirt collar.
tips.why: A bulky knot crowds a small collar.

tips.text: Tie a firm, neat knot and pinch a small dimple below it.
tips.why: A loose knot looks sloppy; the dimple adds polish.

tips.text: Keep the tie darker than the shirt; avoid a light tie on a dark shirt.
tips.why: A pale tie on a dark shirt looks cheap.

tips.text: The tie's tip should reach the top of the trouser waistband when you stand.
Give every tie accessory a job, such as a collar bar holding the knot; when in doubt, take one off.
Never wear a pocket square that matches the tie.
Use a four-in-hand knot rather than a full Windsor.
tips.why: The writer finds the Windsor too bulky.

tips.text: With a pinstripe suit, keep the shirt and tie fairly plain.
tips.why: Let the pinstripe be the pattern that leads.

outfits.outfit: shirt pink smart +fine-stripe +stripes, tie pink smart formal +silk +stripes, jacket navy smart +suit, trousers navy smart +suit
outfits.why: A fine-striped shirt under a wider-striped tie in the same colour, on a plain navy suit as the neutral base.
